outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.reason: Salesforce (+7.5%), ServiceNow (+8.3%), and Palantir (+6.4%) all rallied sharply as money rotated out of AI-infrastructure/chip spending plays and into software names that are starting to show they can monetize AI (Agentforce and ServiceNow AI revenue both reportedly scaling fast).

Ouster and other robot-sensor and component makers surged (Ouster +15.6%) on supply-chain optimism, even as the pure-play humanoid stock in this tracker (UBTECH) stayed roughly flat — a sign the strength is concentrated in components rather than broad-based yet.

weakest.area: Memory chips & the Asian semiconductor supply chain
weakest.reason: Samsung and SK Hynix posted their worst single-day declines in nearly two decades, dragging Korea's Kospi down over 10% and Japan's Nikkei down as much as 4%, on renewed China chip-competition fears and jitters over reported large AI-financing deals; Micron, AMD, and Nvidia all fell in sympathy.
Bitcoin (-2.8%) and Ethereum (-3.3%) both pulled back as the chip-sector selloff spilled into broader risk assets heading into Fed week, with market fear-sentiment readings staying subdued.

outlook.nextStep: Wednesday brings two major catalysts back-to-back — the Fed's rate decision (2pm ET, the new chair's first meeting) and Microsoft's earnings after the close — both worth watching closely rather than acting on ahead of time. Today's split between a crashing chip sector and a rallying software sector is the more textured, worth-a-closer-look signal, since it reflects a real reallocation across the AI trade rather than a single-name story.

signals.title: Asian memory-chip crash drags Samsung and SK Hynix to their worst day in nearly two decades
signals.body: Samsung Electronics closed down roughly 13.4% and SK Hynix fell about 14.7%, pulling Korea's Kospi down over 10% and Japan's Nikkei down as much as 4% to its lowest level since May. The rout was driven by signs of progress in Chinese advanced chipmaking plus jitters over reports that a major AI customer is seeking a large financing backstop from a leading chipmaker, reviving worries about the sustainability of AI-capex spending. Nasdaq 100 futures fell nearly 1% in sympathy.
signals.watch: SK Hynix's next earnings print and any further headlines on Chinese chip-equipment progress or AI-infrastructure financing deals.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — this is a much sharper, more broad-based move than the single-stock pullbacks seen recently, and it's dated and specific rather than vague AI-slowdown chatter.

signals.title: Enterprise software stages a coordinated rebound as money rotates out of AI infrastructure
signals.body: Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Palantir all jumped sharply even on a day when chip stocks were falling hard, as investors rotated from companies spending heavily to build AI toward companies showing they can use AI to grow revenue. Agentforce and ServiceNow's AI products were both cited as scaling quickly.
signals.watch: Whether the rotation holds through the week's remaining earnings (Microsoft Wednesday, Amazon Thursday) or reverses once AI-infrastructure fears cool.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a multi-name, cross-company rally on the same day chips are selling off looks like a real reallocation rather than one company's news.

signals.title: Fed decision Wednesday is the new chair's first meeting, with oil-driven inflation risk still in play
signals.body: The Fed's July 28-29 meeting concludes Wednesday at 2pm ET with a press conference to follow — the first meeting under the recently installed Fed chair, who has signaled less forward guidance than his predecessor. Consensus expects rates held at 3.5-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, but crude oil's roughly 20% rise for the month keeps a headline-inflation scare alive.
signals.watch: Wednesday's 2pm ET rate decision and press conference tone, especially any signal on how the new chair plans to communicate going forward.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a first meeting under new leadership plus elevated oil-driven inflation risk is a lot of event risk to sit in front of.

signals.title: Microsoft heads into Wednesday's earnings with options pricing a 7% move
signals.body: Microsoft reports fiscal Q4 results after the close Wednesday, with analysts expecting EPS of $4.24 (+16% year over year) and revenue near $87.6 billion (+15%). Wall Street's focus is on Azure growth, AI-services demand, and whether heavy data-center capex is translating into returns.
signals.watch: Azure growth rate and any updated capex guidance on the earnings call.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a large, dated catalyst that will likely set the tone for AI-infrastructure sentiment into month-end.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum pull back as chip-sector selloff spills into broader risk assets
signals.body: Bitcoin fell to around $63,200 (-2.8%) and Ethereum to about $1,872 (-3.3%), giving back some of last week's relative calm as the memory-chip crash pushed broader risk sentiment lower heading into the Fed decision.
signals.watch: Whether crypto continues trading in sympathy with tech-equity risk-off moves through the Fed announcement, or decouples again once the meeting passes.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a pullback that tracks a broader risk-off day is less informative than an isolated, crypto-specific move would be.

signals.title: Humanoid-robot component makers surge on supply-chain optimism
signals.body: Robot-sensor and component makers including Ouster jumped double digits on reports of improving supply-chain conditions for humanoid-robot production, even as the pure-play humanoid name in this tracker, UBTECH, stayed roughly flat and Teradyne sat still ahead of its own earnings report today.
signals.watch: Teradyne's earnings today for a read on AI-related test-equipment demand, and whether the component rally broadens to UBTECH and other humanoid-adjacent names.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a sharp, dated move in components is a useful early signal, though it hasn't yet spread to the pure-play names.

signals.title: Cybersecurity holds recent gains on continued analyst price-target hikes
signals.body: CrowdStrike and peers have continued to hold up on AI-security demand, with multiple analysts raising price targets in recent weeks (one to $230, another to $235) citing strength across identity, SIEM, and AI-driven detection products.
signals.watch: Whether the group's relative strength persists through upcoming peer earnings and any follow-through from recent partnership announcements.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — this remains a multi-week pattern of analyst upgrades rather than a single day's move.
